newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi says Italy can bring stability to euro.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi says Italy can bring stability to euro.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said a delay to economic and monetary union (EMU) would be a political defeat for Europe and vowed that Italy could bring stability to the single currency.

"The delay of the euro regarding the 1999 deadline would be a political defeat for Europe, a victory for those who want a weak and divided Europe unable to face up to the role that history asks of it," he said.
His comments were made in a speech at an exhibition entitled "Building Europe together: From the lira to the euro"
Ciampi said Italy, as other EU countries, was making "a great effort" to join the single currency.
"The effort is not only...in reaching the quantative, nominal respect for the convergence parameters. The parameters are simply points of reference," he said.
"The convergence that we are aiming for above all is the deeper one that affects the structures, which demand reform."
Ciampi said much had been done in this direction, citing fiscal reform, reform of public administration and state finances as well as of the judicial system.
"Italy's desire...to participate in the single currency is based on the knowledge that the member countries must be in a position to bring stability to the euro," he said.
"Italy knows it is in such a position."
Ciampi said the euro was a "fundamental step" in the development of the European Union and the single currency must be stable to be an instrument of growth.

"We are well aware of the importance of a currency's stability," he said. "Stability is an essential condition to encourage savings, to generate and make available for business initiatives ample resources at low rates of interest."
The Maastricht Treaty demands a deficit/GDP ratio of three percent for countries wishing to sign up to EMU when it is launched in 1999.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi earlier repeated the government position that Italy was eager to join EMU and was not seeking any delay to the launch of the single currency.
